title: Adult CPR and AED practice: compact grounding dataset
artifact_type: Self-contained, paraphrased reference facts plus separately labeled prototype design. Not an official AHA/Red Cross course, published dataset, or certification rubric.
intended_use: Ground a conversational AI instructor during a supervised manikin demonstration; suitable for prompt context or retrieval. No external files are required to interpret this file.
clinical_review_status: Source-checked by the assistant; not reviewed or validated by a qualified CPR instructor.

scope.patient: Adult sudden collapse without trauma, drowning or other special circumstance; manikin simulation only.
scope.learner: Lay rescuer, not a healthcare-professional BLS certification candidate.
scope.optional_mode: trained_lay_with_breaths; enable only with an instructor-approved lesson and suitable manikin/barrier equipment.
not_covered: traumatic arrest or combat casualty care
scope.boundary: These exclusions define a narrow demo, not situations where CPR is unnecessary. Do not extrapolate the module into an omitted clinical protocol.
practice_equipment: adult CPR manikin, preferably with validated feedback
AED trainer if AED actions are practiced
simulation_rules: Never practice chest compressions on a healthy volunteer.
Use a non-shocking AED trainer in the demo.
Simulate emergency calls; do not actually dial 911 for practice.
Have a qualified CPR instructor check the exercise before learner use.
scope.real_emergency_boundary: If a real emergency is reported, end simulation framing, advise calling 911/local emergency services immediately and following dispatcher/AED guidance. Do not delay emergency action for app setup, questions, camera positioning or lesson completion.

facts.text: For lay rescuers, unresponsiveness plus absent breathing or gasping indicates presumed cardiac arrest; gasping is not normal breathing.
Lay recognition does not require pulse palpation; healthcare professionals limit their pulse assessment to ten seconds.
A lone rescuer activates emergency response, then starts compressions immediately; speakerphone can support nearly simultaneous action.
Compression-only CPR is appropriate for lay rescuers untrained or unwilling to give breaths. Trained rescuers are encouraged to include breaths.
Overlap the hands, placing the lower hand’s heel centrally over the lower half to lower third of the sternum.
For an average adult, reach at least five centimeters; avoid exceeding six centimeters.
Use a compression cadence between one hundred and one hundred twenty per minute.
Let the chest fully rebound; avoid residual leaning between compressions.
Check scene safety and responsiveness promptly; assess breathing for no longer than ten seconds. Use available protective equipment.
In the United States, call 911 and obtain an AED, delegating these tasks when another person is available.
Practice with the manikin face-up on a firm, flat surface, kneeling alongside; keep shoulders above hands and elbows straight.

For trained rescuers giving breaths: use 30 compressions followed by two breaths. Open the airway with head tilt/chin lift; create a seal. Give each breath over about one second, enough for chest rise. Reposition and reseal if the first breath fails to raise the chest.
Keep compression interruptions under ten seconds and use an AED promptly when available.

Turn on the AED and obey its prompts. Expose and dry the chest; follow pad illustrations. Typical adult placement is upper-right chest and left side below the armpit. Connect the cable if the device requires it.
Ensure nobody touches the person during rhythm analysis or shock delivery. Deliver a shock only when the AED directs it.
Restart compressions immediately after a shock or a no-shock decision. Continue following device instructions.

Continue until signs of life appear, the scene becomes unsafe, exhaustion prevents continuation, or another trained responder or EMS takes over. When an AED is ready, follow its analysis/shock prompts, then resume as directed.
When another rescuer is available, alternate compressors every one to two minutes, minimizing the transition pause.
CPR feedback devices are recommended for training; unaided visual judgments of compression quality are often unreliable.
Include booster practice after a concentrated course; distributing learning over separate sessions is also reasonable.
The detailed recommendation table allows considering AR for real-time CPR feedback; it does not validate this glasses prototype.

prototype_coaching.kind: Authored application design; not a clinical guideline or validated teaching protocol.
rules: Load scope, source policy and observation limits with retrieved facts; never retrieve isolated numbers without adult/audience context.
Use one short spoken correction at a time. Put one matching cue on the HUD.
Explain during briefing or debriefing. Do not require answers to coaching questions while the learner is actively performing timed compressions.
Do not interrupt the activity merely to capture a better image. Mark the view insufficient and review positioning between practice attempts.
Apply breaths criteria only in the explicitly selected trained-rescuer mode. Do not penalize omitted breaths in compression-only mode.
Offer an optional metronome from a local audio/timer component using the rate fact. The cue is not evidence of the learner’s actual cadence.
Separate coaching practice from an assessment attempt; record when hints were given.
After an attempt, select one observed weakness, give a brief correction, and repeat a comparable exercise. Compare only metrics measured by the same method.
Do not invent a diagnosis, shock recommendation, survival probability, certification result or overall clinical competence score.

observation_limits.kind: Engineering constraints for this prototype, informed by the feedback evidence; not measurements validated for these glasses.
observation_limits.camera_can_support: Qualitative observations of visible hand placement, setup, pad locations and contact during AED simulation, only when the relevant area is clearly visible.
camera_cannot_certify: all bystanders being clear when outside the field of view
observation_limits.cadence: Do not estimate compression cadence from sparse video samples such as one frame per second. Require manikin telemetry or a separately validated measurement stream with timestamps.
evidence_rules: Treat learner statements as self-report, not observed performance.
Treat exercise-engine patient state as simulated, not camera-detected.
Attach timestamps and evidence type to every assessment finding.
Use unknown when evidence is missing or occluded; unknown is not failure.
Use sensor data only if the sensor measures that metric and the stream is current; missing telemetry must not become zero.

practice_rubric.kind: Authored checklist for a demo, not an official certification assessment.
practice_rubric.grading: Report findings by criterion; no composite pass mark. Never score a sensor-only criterion from camera appearance.

criteria.evidence: Spoken decisions and simulated call/AED request events.
Clear view or instructor observation; otherwise unknown.
Validated feedback manikin or validated measurement stream only.
Continuous trustworthy event timing; distinguish device-directed pauses from unrelated interruptions.
Instructor observation or suitable manikin feedback; not applicable in compression-only mode.
AED-trainer events plus visible actions; do not infer unseen contact.
Learner decision against explicit simulated patient/device state.

demo_scenario.kind: Synthetic, authored practice fixture; not patient data.

initial_state.aed: trainer available after a simulated request

demo_scenario.state_delivery: Announce these as simulation facts. Do not claim the glasses detected responsiveness or breathing in a plastic manikin.

flow.instruction: Explain chosen mode and equipment; show how simulated calls and AED requests work.
Use measured feedback where available; keep unmeasured metrics unknown.
Follow the actual trainer prompts; skip physical pad grading if no trainer is present.
Show one supported strength, one supported improvement and what could not be measured.
Repeat the selected weakness with fewer hints. Do not manufacture a better score.

demo_scenario.end_condition: Instructor ends the practice. This is a simulation stopping rule, not a recommendation to stop CPR in an emergency.

agent_checks.kind: Authored grounding checks, not a clinical exam.
